entries.name: tracking.maneuverability_noise

entries.name: scanning.boltzmann_constant
entries.reference: SI 2019 exact definition
entries.rationale: Boltzmann constant k = 1.380649e-23 J/K; a standard physical constant, not a fitted parameter.

entries.name: tracking.initialization_policy
entries.rationale: DEGENERATE GEOMETRY: the paper initializes the estimate at the origin, where the range/azimuth measurement is singular (atan2(0, 0) undefined; measurement Jacobian degenerate). 'paper_zero_identity' reproduces the paper and is retained as a documented DIAGNOSTIC mode; it must never silently produce NaN/inf or an artificial Jacobian (an update at the origin raises MeasurementGeometryError).
notes: M3 review (instruction 3.3): the OPERATIONAL estimator uses the 'measurement_driven' policy, initializing from the first supplied observation plus explicitly configured velocity prior assumptions; the true state is never accessible to initialization.
No numerical initial-covariance values are attributed to the paper beyond x0 = 0, P0 = I_4.

entries.name: tracking.measurement_driven_initial_velocity
entries.reference: M3 review instruction 9 (no paper value)
entries.rationale: Velocity prior MEAN for measurement-driven initialization. Unresolved by default (None): initialization raises an informative error rather than inventing a default. Synthetic experiments supply values labeled as synthetic settings.

entries.name: tracking.measurement_driven_initial_velocity_variance
entries.reference: M3 review instruction 9 (no paper value)
entries.rationale: Velocity prior VARIANCE per axis (isotropic) for measurement-driven initialization; kept conceptually separate from the position uncertainty, which is derived from the first observation's covariance. Unresolved by default (None).

entries.name: tracking.covariance_update_method
entries.rationale: NUMERICAL STABILITY option: default 'paper_equation_13' applies Eq. (13) as printed, P_{t|t} = (I - K_t H_t) P_{t|t-1}. 'joseph' uses the form-preserving PSD update P = (I-KH) P (I-KH)^T + K R K^T, mathematically equivalent for the exact Kalman gain; equivalence is tested under valid numerical conditions.
notes: Posterior covariances are symmetrized against floating-point drift; covariance eigenvalues are never clipped to conceal defects.

entries.name: tracking.measurement_variance_semantics
entries.value: sigma^2_{r|theta,t} = sigma^2_{r|theta,0} / SNR_t (reference variance divided by linear SNR)
entries.reference: Z. Lu et al., IEEE ICC 2024, DOI 10.1109/ICC51166.2024.10622225; Eq. (6) and surrounding prose, p. 2787
entries.rationale: Owner-reviewed reading of Eq. (6). Evidence: (a) the paper prose directly below Eq. (6) states the variance DECREASES with longer dwell time or closer target 'according to equations (5) and (6)'; (b) SNR grows with dwell time and proximity per Eq. (5); (c) standard radar behaviour. Only the inverse reading satisfies all three.
notes: EXTRACTION HISTORY (settled): an early plain-text PDF extraction juxtaposed sigma^2_{.,0} and SNR_t on one line, producing a transient multiplication reading that contradicted the same paper's prose. Re-inspection with layout-aware extraction and the M3/M4 reviews identified this as a PDF-EXTRACTION ARTIFACT, not an unresolved mathematical ambiguity; the division semantics is the accepted paper reading and inverse-SNR scaling is NOT classified as a proposed deviation.
Implemented in radar_bo/radar/measurement_noise.py; requires the unresolved SNR0 (see tracking.reference_snr).

entries.name: optimization.kernel
entries.reference: M. Benzaghta et al., IEEE GLOBECOM 2023, DOI 10.1109/GLOBECOM54140.2023.10437768
entries.rationale: Matern-5/2 kernel; our harness is a methodological adaptation, not an exact reproduction of that paper's algorithm (README research foundations).

entries.name: optimization.acquisition_xi
entries.reference: M. Benzaghta et al., IEEE GLOBECOM 2023, DOI 10.1109/GLOBECOM54140.2023.10437768
entries.rationale: Expected-improvement exploration parameter xi = 0.01 reported by Benzaghta et al. NOT carried as a configuration field: the installed BoTorch LogExpectedImprovement (verified at runtime) accepts NO exploration-offset parameter, so the M5 engine uses conventional LogEI without xi. This entry preserves the paper value in the provenance record only (methodological adaptation); no no-effect configuration parameter is retained.

entries.name: optimization.num_acquisition_candidates
entries.reference: M. Benzaghta et al., IEEE GLOBECOM 2023, DOI 10.1109/GLOBECOM54140.2023.10437768
entries.rationale: Acquisition candidate pool Nc = 500 per iteration.

entries.name: optimization.search_mode
entries.reference: M. Benzaghta et al., IEEE GLOBECOM 2023, DOI 10.1109/GLOBECOM54140.2023.10437768
entries.rationale: 'joint' is the default harness mode. Benzaghta et al. update one BS at a time (block-wise); 'alternating' mirrors that scheme and 'coordinate' is experimental.
notes: Adaptation, not reproduction: the paper's block-wise scheme is per-BS in their problem, not a generic harness mode.

entries.name: scanning.area_ratio_metric
entries.rationale: Eq. (21) implemented as a pure metric accepting a modeled detectable area and a strictly positive reference area; the ratio is NOT capped at one. Physical scanning calculations (Eqs. (16)-(20)) are NOT implemented: their parameters are unspecified (Table I).
notes: The paper's S0 remains unresolved (scanning.reference_area); the metric raises a parameter-resolution error rather than substituting a default.

entries.name: resource.remaining_scanning_time_convention
entries.rationale: Paper's own nonnegative remaining-time convention implemented verbatim in the resource accountant. The RAW time deficit is recorded alongside so an over-budget allocation is never silently made valid by the clipping; feasibility is judged separately by the constraint manager.
notes: M4: an allocation violating the proposed hard per-slot budget is reported infeasible; the Eq. (24) clipping does not rescue it.

entries.name: objective.eq23_aggregation
entries.rationale: Aggregation structure implemented by the objective evaluator over explicit component interfaces (tracking-cost provider, scanning-performance model). No GP training, acquisition optimization or BO candidate generation inside the evaluator.
notes: Single-slot objective; the paper's long-term discounted CMDP objective remains a recorded deviation (README section 14).

entries.name: resource.task_utility_weights
entries.reference: Z. Lu et al., IEEE ICC 2024, DOI 10.1109/ICC51166.2024.10622225; Eq. (23) weights w_n
entries.rationale: Per-task weights of the weighted tracking aggregate. None (default) means UNIFORM weights - a proposed software default, NOT a paper value. When supplied, weights must be finite, non-negative and match the task count.

entries.name: scanning.synthetic_linear_scanning_model
entries.rationale: SYNTHETIC scanning response S_det(tau_s) = k_synth * tau_s with gamma = S_det / S0_synth, for software integration tests ONLY. Constants are synthetic testing values, not radar physics; outputs must never be presented as validated coverage, detectable range or detection probability.
notes: Deterministic; documented numerical domain tau_s >= 0 finite; invalid inputs rejected.

entries.name: objective.randomness_policy
entries.rationale: Candidate evaluations rebuild the NumPy generator from the snapshot's CAPTURED state, so all candidates see identical random realizations and evaluation order cannot change outcomes. An independent-realizations policy would draw fresh entropy per evaluation; CRN is the documented M4 default and is recorded in every evaluation result.

entries.name: allocation.discrete_membership_policy
entries.rationale: Flat-vector dwell values must match the configured action set EXACTLY (tolerance 1e-12); near-members are rejected with the nearest member reported for diagnosis. No snapping, rounding, clipping or repair (M4 instruction 9).

entries.name: objective.snapshot_truth_exclusion
entries.rationale: The frozen snapshot carries posterior means/covariances, time, task ids and the captured generator state; TRUE simulated states are deliberately NOT copied into snapshots, so candidate-evaluation components cannot receive ground truth through the snapshot interface. Truth stays in the authoritative SimulationState.
notes: Snapshot integrity is content-hashed (sha256) and re-verified after every evaluation.

entries.name: objective.tracking_provider_m4_scope
entries.rationale: M4 tracking-cost retrieval uses the paper's Eq. (14) on the snapshot's CURRENT posteriors - allocation-independent by design. A candidate's effect on FUTURE tracking requires simulation advancement (M5+); a synthetic allocation-dependent provider exists for aggregation testing only (clearly labeled synthetic).

entries.name: bo.problem_interface.scope
entries.rationale: The generic problem interface (dimension, variable names/types/bounds, discrete values, instantaneous feasibility, scalar objective, direction, noise declaration, evaluation ids) imports NOTHING from the radar/environment/simulation layers (enforced by test_layer_separation). Evaluation ids have the format '{problem_id}_eval_{counter:05d}_{uuid8}'.

entries.name: bo.benchmarks.a_b_c.origin
entries.rationale: Benchmarks A/B/C are synthetic problems defined in M5 to VERIFY the generic BO engine (analytic/enumeration-checkable optima). They are NOT taken from Benzaghta et al. or Lu et al.; the M4 diagnostic tracking provider is NOT used as a BO benchmark (M5 instruction 5).

entries.name: bo.benchmark_a.reference
entries.rationale: Synthetic continuous quadratic benchmark A: f(u,v) = 10 - (u-3.5)^2 - (v-7.2)^2 on [-10,10]^2, maximize. Analytic exact reference derived independently (vertex of the concave quadratic); verified by tests with math.isclose.
notes: verification_method = analytic_exact; used as the BO gap reference in the M5 validation experiment.

entries.name: bo.benchmark_b.reference
entries.rationale: Synthetic constrained mixed-variable benchmark B: discrete d in {0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0}, continuous x in [0,10], constraint x + 3d <= 8, objective f = 4d + x^2/4 (maximize). Enumeration over the 4 discrete values with the analytic clamped inner optimum (x* = min(10, 8 - 3d)) gives per-d optima 3.0/6.0/9.0/11.0; f* = 11.0 at (d=2.0, x=2.0).
notes: verification_method = enumeration_exact (per-d values independently derived).

entries.name: bo.benchmark_c.reference
entries.value: numerical_approximate (computed by the reference solver at run time)
entries.rationale: Synthetic multimodal benchmark C on [-2.5,2.5]^2 (sum of Gaussian bumps). NO analytic optimum is claimed: the reference is computed numerically (differential evolution plus a dense grid scan) by an independent solver and recorded with the result; it may be exceeded by BO because it is approximate.
notes: verification_method = numerical_approximate; the reference VALUE is never assumed, only computed and recorded.

entries.name: bo.duplicate_tolerance
entries.rationale: Exact-match tolerance for duplicate-configuration detection (dataset insert and pool generation). Deterministic problems never re-evaluate a known configuration; noisy problems may repeat deliberately (allow_duplicates). Duplicates are never silently merged.

entries.name: bo.feasibility_tolerance
entries.rationale: Numerical tolerance of the instantaneous constraint check in the generic problem interface. Synthetic problems define their OWN explicit constraints (M4 review 3.1: per-action feasibility is distinct from discounted-budget feasibility).

entries.name: bo.consecutive_failure_cap
entries.rationale: Maximum consecutive objective/GP-fitting failures before the loop stops (prevents unlimited failure loops; failures consume budget by documented policy).

entries.name: bo.initial_design_sampling
entries.rationale: The initial design is seeded uniform random sampling over the feasible region (provisional size 30, README BOConfig experimental). Deliberately NOT Latin hypercube or Sobol (explicit M5 instruction: initial design is random sampling, distinct from the acquisition search).

entries.name: bo.refit_policy
entries.rationale: M5 initial GP-fitting policy: a fresh fit_gpytorch_mll refit after each successful new observation (no warm-start; warm-starting would be a different, explicitly identified and tested strategy).

entries.name: bo.selection_policy
entries.rationale: Candidates are scored as a batch of single candidates (k, 1, d) against the installed single-candidate LogExpectedImprovement (q=1 verified at runtime); selection is argmax over FINITE log-domain scores with deterministic first-index tie-breaking; non-finite scores are masked and reported, never repaired.

entries.name: bo.failures_policy
entries.rationale: Failed objective-evaluation attempts consume the evaluation budget (real evaluation cost), are recorded as explicit failure records with preserved tracebacks, and NEVER enter the training dataset (M4 review 3.2 semantics).

entries.name: bo.incumbent_policy
entries.rationale: The incumbent is the best successfully OBSERVED feasible configuration (exact vector preserved); it is NEVER replaced by an unevaluated GP prediction. Termination is never described as proof of global convergence.

entries.name: experiment.m5_synthetic_validation_budget
entries.rationale: Provisional synthetic budgets for the M5 generic-validation experiment only (benchmarks A/B/C x seeds 0-9 x BO vs random search). Not paper-derived; the general evaluation_budget remains UNRESOLVED and is set per experiment.

entries.name: bo.blocks.representation
entries.rationale: A block names an ordered subset of decision-variable indices; block metadata (ids, active/fixed indices) is recorded as evaluation metadata, NEVER as GP input features. Blocks must not overlap; uncovered variables stay fixed at the current configuration and are reported. Full coverage is validated only when required.

entries.name: bo.scheduling.strategy
entries.rationale: Blocks are visited in given order, repeating; one complete cycle = every block visited or skipped once. Joint = one full-dimension block (M5 baseline); alternating = two user-defined blocks; pair-wise ('coordinate') = at least two two-variable blocks (two two-variable blocks match both readings; the declared search_mode resolves the ambiguity).

entries.name: bo.current_config_vs_incumbent
entries.rationale: The CURRENT CONFIGURATION is the feasible complete vector around which block candidates are built; the GLOBAL INCUMBENT is the best successfully evaluated feasible configuration of the whole run. Both always refer to actual stored observations; neither is ever replaced by an unevaluated GP prediction; they are maintained independently and may differ.

entries.name: bo.acceptance_policy
entries.rationale: PROPOSED implementation choice: the current configuration is updated only when a verified evaluation improves its value by more than the configured tolerance improvement_tolerance (default 0). Exploratory evaluations that do not improve remain in the shared dataset. Non-improving-acceptance policies are separate experiments, not mixed with the primary comparison.

entries.name: bo.evaluations_per_block_visit
entries.rationale: Primary M6 strategy: ONE acquisition-selected evaluation per block visit (which is NOT an exact block maximization). Configurable for later experiments; all evaluations share the global budget.

entries.name: bo.full_gp_dimension_vs_block_dimension
entries.rationale: ONE shared GP trains on ALL successful COMPLETE configurations (M x d, full dimension) regardless of active block size; only the acquisition-SEARCH dimension shrinks per block. Reducing the block dimension does not reduce GP training cost. Separate per-block GPs would be a distinct, unapproved method.

entries.name: bo.benchmark_stagnation_lp.reference
entries.rationale: Synthetic block-stagnation LP (dim 4): max 3a1 + b1 + 3a2 + b2 s.t. a1+b1+a2+b2 <= 3.2, all in [0, 1.6]. Analytic exact LP optimum 9.6 at (1.6, 0, 1.6, 0) via the fractional-knapsack greedy argument. From budget-tight configurations the alternating a/b grouping provably cannot improve while the joint optimum exists (demonstrated in tests).

entries.name: bo.highdim_benchmarks.origin
entries.rationale: M6 synthetic benchmarks in dimensions 4/8/16: separable quadratic (analytic exact f* = 10d), coupled quadratic via fixed PD mixing matrix (analytic exact f* = 20), constrained mixed 2-discrete + continuous with shared budget (numerical_approximate reference via enumeration + KKT multiplier bisection), and the block-stagnation LP (analytic exact). All parameters synthetic; none from the reference papers.

entries.name: experiment.m6_block_architecture_budget
entries.rationale: Primary M6 comparison settings inherited from M5: budget 100 total ATTEMPTED objective evaluations (NOT per block), initial design 30, pool 500 per search, seeds 0-9. The budget is shared across architectures for fairness.

entries.name: optimization.num_initial_observations
entries.rationale: Initial space-filling design size; no paper default (README BOConfig proposes 30).

entries.name: optimization.evaluation_budget
entries.rationale: UNRESOLVED by design: no paper default; each experiment must set it explicitly (OptimizationConfig.ensure_ready fails clearly otherwise).

entries.name: environment.num_targets
entries.rationale: Fixed-population synthetic scenario (README 4.4); paper's population is not specified for reproduction.

entries.name: environment.random_seed
entries.rationale: Master seed for reproducibility; per-repetition seeds derived deterministically.

entries.name: experiment.repetitions
entries.rationale: Independent repetitions for statistical reporting; no paper default.

entries.name: resource.time_budget_semantics
entries.rationale: Default reproduces the paper's discounted cumulative budget. The proposed 'hard_per_slot' alternative is STRICTER (per-slot bound vs discounted cumulative bound); recorded as a deviation whenever used.
notes: M3 review (instruction 3.4): 'hard_per_slot' is reserved for the proposed BO configuration profile (M4+); no resource allocation or budget optimization is implemented in M3.

entries.name: experiment.m7_runner_architecture
entries.rationale: M7 experiment runner: per-run atomic JSON records (tmp + os.replace), manifest with explicit statuses (pending/running/completed/failed/skipped + reasons), resume compatibility verified against configuration fingerprint, benchmark/algorithm versions, dependency versions, seeds and run ids; corrupted/incompatible records are REJECTED, never silently combined.
notes: Layer separation: the experiment layer never carries radar configuration.

entries.name: experiment.m7_shared_initialization_policy
entries.rationale: Fairness (item 10): all methods for one (benchmark, seed) run with the same seed through the same deterministic sampler; the runner then VERIFIES identical initial configurations AND identical observed values directly from the stored records (seeds alone are never trusted). Random search has no initial-design phase by construction and is excluded from the comparison, reported explicitly.
notes: Deviation documented: initial designs are NOT injected into the engine; the engine's seeded sampler IS the shared design, verified post hoc from records.

entries.name: experiment.m7_statistical_conventions
entries.rationale: M7 statistics: paired comparisons preserve seed-level pairing; ties use the engine duplicate tolerance 1e-9; bootstrap resamples COMPLETE seed-level pairs with a documented seed (2026) and B=10000; Wilcoxon two-sided signed-rank on non-zero differences, Holm-corrected when presented as a family; p-values complement effect sizes and CIs and never imply practical significance alone.
notes: Descriptive over 10 seeds; a narrow interval is NOT evidence of universal superiority.

entries.name: experiment.m7_threshold_definitions
entries.rationale: M7 threshold metrics: fractions of the INITIAL REFERENCE GAP (0.5/0.9/0.99 by default), frozen before new comparative experiments; unreached thresholds are reported explicitly (never interpolated); the initial-design-already-meets case is flagged. Distinct from the M6 threshold convention (fraction of f*).

entries.name: experiment.m7_runtime_accounting
entries.rationale: M7 runtime decomposition: five disjoint stage timers (GP fit, candidate generation, feasibility validation, acquisition scoring, objective evaluation) plus explicit unattributed overhead = wall - sum(components). FINDING: the archived M6 generation timer INCLUDED nested feasibility validation; the boundary is fixed for M7+ records (disjoint), historical values are preserved unchanged and corrected only in derived artifacts. The decomposition is never claimed to sum exactly to wall time.
notes: Serialization, tensor conversion, dataset insertion, incumbent tracking and GP training-tensor preparation are NOT separately timed.

entries.name: experiment.m7_candidate_profiling_baseline
entries.rationale: M6 candidate-generation algorithm is preserved UNCHANGED as the versioned baseline; profiling distinguishes PROVEN finite-space exhaustion (all-discrete blocks with enumerable combinations) from sampling failure (continuous spaces: an empty pool does not prove an empty feasible set). Any future faster generator must be a new explicitly versioned implementation.
notes: M6 measured (mean across 10 seeds, constrained_mixed_8d): alternating generation 251.5 s incl. nested feasibility 67.4 s (corrected derived value 184.1 s); joint 77.4 s; pairwise 103.9 s.

entries.name: experiment.m7_validation_matrix
entries.rationale: M7 limited validation matrix (item 26): benchmark_a (2-D) + constrained_mixed_8d, methods RS/joint/alternating/pairwise/reference, seeds 0-2, budget 40 total (initial 10). Purpose: validate the INFRASTRUCTURE (runner, checkpoint/resume, metrics, reporting), NOT algorithm superiority. The 230 archived M6 runs are NOT repeated.
notes: Manifest records 2 incompatible combinations as skipped with reasons (benchmark_a defines no recommended block groupings).

entries.name: experiment.m7_milestone_reconciliation
entries.rationale: Milestone numbering reconciliation: the original README roadmap has EIGHT milestones (M1 repo/env, M2 config/provenance, M3 estimation, M4 interfaces, M5 generic BO, M6 verification of BO components, M7 architectures validation, M8 runner package + analysis, M9 final docs in the instruction stream). The instruction stream's M7 (experimental framework) maps onto the README roadmap's M8 'runner package' plus parts of M7 'analysis extensions'; the instruction stream carries one additional milestone (M9 final documentation) beyond the roadmap's eight. Every deviation is documented in the README.
notes: No milestone renumbering was applied to existing artifacts; existing archives keep their original M5/M6 labels.

entries.name: experiment.m8a_run_count_reconciliation
entries.rationale: M8A item 3.2 reconciliation: the durable M6 full-matrix archive contains exactly 220 records (160 primary = 4 benchmarks x 4 methods x 10 seeds + 60 dimension-study = 2 x 3 x 10) and the pilot archive 32 records. The '230 runs' figure quoted in the M6/M7 narrative summaries was an ARITHMETIC/REPORTING ERROR (correct count 220); the archives themselves were always internally consistent and were validated as such by the M7 independent checks. No records are missing or invented.
notes: Corrected via documentation only; historical archive values untouched.

entries.name: experiment.m8a_shared_initial_design_interface
entries.rationale: M8A item 3.3: BayesianOptimizer accepts initial_design_configs (validated immutable explicit shared design: exact count, dimension, finiteness and feasibility enforced fail-fast; input never mutated; pool report records the explicit mode with zero sampling cost). The experiment framework gains initial_design.mode='explicit_shared': one deterministic design per (benchmark, dimension, seed) is generated from the registry sampler and passed UNCHANGED to every applicable method, guaranteeing identical initial configurations AND observed values by construction (still verified from stored records). Default None preserves M5/M6 seeded behavior bit-for-bit (frozen-trajectory regression test passes unchanged).
notes: Historical optimization trajectories and archives are unaffected.
